oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: cross-region routing anomaly. Elevated 5xx rate and tail latency for requests routed to ap-southeast. Auto-page: sarah (oncall). Collecting initial telemetry.
oncall-bot: Links: https://telemetry/redwood/incidents/2245012345, runbooks: #incidents/runbooks/routing
sarah: seeing spikes in 5xx starting ~2245012300 UTC. Affected frontend -> generations service + embeddings.
sarah: pinging @raj for DNS/routing deep-dive — can you grab resolver traces?
raj: on it. Initial quick check: `dig +short api.redwood.internal @8.8.8.8` returns mix of IPs (ap-southeast and eu-west). TTLs look low (~30s) but caches are inconsistent across ASes.
raj: curl from eu-west node: `curl -sv https://api.redwood.internal/health` -> OK. From ap-southeast node: high latency, some requests get 502. Trace shows requests hitting eu-west nodes causing timeouts due to cross-region egress limits.
mike: whether a recent routing policy push could explain this? I see a rollout earlier today for latency-steering weights. @ops-bot can you show last routing policy deploy?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-service v2.14.3 promoted by emily at 2245011000 UTC. Change: added latency-weighted fallthrough for ap-southeast. Diff: `+prefer-eu-on-latency-fallback` (id: pr-842)
emily: I approved that earlier but didn't expect cache-coherence issues. Looks like some edge caches saw the new policy while others didn't, causing split-horizon.
sarah: mitigation plan: 1) roll back latency-weighted change to immediate fallback, 2) pin ap-southeast for currently active sessions, 3) flush DNS caches in key egress clusters.
raj: rolling back policy now. CMD: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://policy-service.internal/api/v1/rollbacks -d '{"policy_id":"pr-842","reason":"inconsistent rollout -> cross-region misroute"}'
```
mike: I'm starting a temporary pin to ap-southeast for `generations` route to avoid cross-region fanout. CMD: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://routing.internal/v1/pins -d '{"service":"generations","region":"ap-southeast-1","expires_in":3600,"note":"emergency pin during rollout inconsistency"}'
```
sarah: initiating DNS cache flush on critical egress nodes: `for host in egress1 egress2 egress3; do ssh $host 'sudo systemctl restart dnsmasq'; done`
emily: notifying CS to prepare outgoing comms. @customer-success assign liaison for impacted customers.
customer-success: notified. Initial impact estimate: 18-24% of ap-southeast traffic saw elevated error/latency for ~10-20m window. Priority customers affected: AcmeApps, Zoomly, DataFarm. Drafting messages.
raj: telemetry update: 5xx rate peaked at 22:40 UTC, error type predominantly 502/504 from cross-region proxies. RTT to eu-west from ap-southeast nodes jumped to 800-1200ms causing timeouts.
sarah: status: rollback applied at 2245012360, pin applied at 2245012375, dns cache restarts kicked at 2245012380. Watching metrics.
mike: after pins and rollback, error rate dropping. 5xx baseline moving toward normal. 
ops-bot: metric-check: 5xx rate from ap-southeast now down 85% relative to peak. Latency p50 back to expected, p99 trending down.
emily: CS update: sent targeted email to top 10 impacted customers, posted status page note draft.
sarah: can we keep pin for 30m and then start a controlled re-rollout with stricter canary?
mike: yes, will schedule a slow ramp with narrower edge-scope. New rollout will include cache-coherence checks and staged DNS TTL increase.
raj: postmortem action items so far: 1) make policy rollouts idempotent across edge caches, 2) add canary gate for DNS visible-flush check, 3) set safer default TTL during rollouts.
sarah: oncall => handoff to mike in 30m for monitoring. Declaring incident mitigated for customers; will keep paging for regressions. :white_check_mark: 
emily: good catch, quick mitigation. preparing retro docs.
customer-success: will follow up with impacted customers with timeline + RCA once postmortem ready.
sarah: closing notes: incident severity: Sev2. Duration: ~20m of customer-impacting errors. Root cause: inconsistent policy rollout -> cache incoherence -> cross-region misroute and timeouts.
oncall-bot: Incident 2245012345 status: mitigated. Postmortem assigned to emily, raj.
